purpose: Legacy-v1 self-consistency receipt for a fleet node reconstruction of an original payload from a k-of-n erasure shard set. It binds contributing shard commitments, the coding parameters actually used, and reconstructing-node metadata, allowing accidental corruption and internally inconsistent reconstruction claims to be detected without the original data.
security_status: Legacy v1 uses the public NodeId bytes as its HMAC key, so it is forgeable and MUST NOT be treated as non-repudiation or trusted Byzantine-blame evidence. Trusted Ed25519 receipt admission and protocol-v2 cutover are tracked by bd-q8x8x.6; this schema documents the isolated legacy carrier only.

coding_scheme.description: The gossip erasure lane is a systematic XOR single-parity code: one parity shard recovers at most one missing data shard. This is NOT Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8); the receipt records the real scheme identifier and (k, n) plan and never fabricates Reed-Solomon polynomial coefficients the implementation does not compute. A wider code would introduce a new scheme id and a new receipt schema version.

determinism: receipt_commitment is a SHA-256 content hash over a length-prefixed canonical preimage. Every variable-length field (schema_id, shard_set_id, coding_scheme, per-shard origin_node, reconstructing_node, extension keys/values) is prefixed with its u64 big-endian byte length before its bytes; fixed-width scalars are big-endian; the ErasureShardRole is a single tag byte (Data=0, Parity=1); the Option<u16> recovery slot carries an explicit tag byte (0 => None, 1 => Some) so None cannot collide with Some(0). Contributing shards are emitted in strictly-increasing shard_index order. Two honest implementations agree byte-for-byte on the commitment, mirroring compute_erasure_shard_hash in the fleet protocol.

receipt_fields.shard_set_id: string; stable identifier shared by all shards of the reconstructed set
receipt_fields.payload_hash: ContentHash (32-byte SHA-256); content hash of the reconstructed original payload
receipt_fields.payload_len: u64; byte length of the reconstructed original payload
receipt_fields.contributing_shards: array of shard_commitment; the shards that materially fed reconstruction (present data shards, plus the parity shard iff a data shard was recovered), in strictly-increasing shard_index order
receipt_fields.recovered_shard_index: Option<u16>; the data-shard index recovered from parity, or null when every data shard was directly present
receipt_fields.reconstructing_node: NodeId; claimed identity of the node that performed the reconstruction; not trusted under the legacy v1 tag
receipt_fields.receipt_commitment: ContentHash (32-byte SHA-256) over the length-prefixed canonical preimage of all fields above
receipt_fields.signature: Legacy-v1 MessageSignature carrier { signer: NodeId, hash: AuthenticityHash }; HMAC-SHA256 tag over receipt_commitment keyed by public reconstructing-node identifier bytes. It provides intrinsic mutation detection only, not signer authentication.
receipt_fields.extensions: map<string,string>; forward-compatible extension fields, sorted and length-prefixed into the commitment

shard_commitment_fields.shard_index: u16; index of the shard within its set
shard_commitment_fields.shard_hash: ContentHash (32-byte SHA-256); the shard's canonical content hash as recorded on the ErasureShard
shard_commitment_fields.origin_node: NodeId; node that originally encoded the shard
shard_commitment_fields.sequence: u64; per-origin sequence number of the shard

verification.verify: ReconstructionReceipt::verify() — validates legacy-v1 intrinsic consistency: schema id, coding scheme, a well-formed plan, exactly k canonically ordered contributors, data/parity index ranges, exactly k data and zero parity without recovery or k-1 data and exactly one parity during recovery, signer metadata coherence, recomputed commitment equality, and the legacy self-contained authentication tag. It requires neither payload nor shards, but it does not establish trusted signer authority.
verification.verify_against_shards: ReconstructionReceipt::verify_against_shards(shards, reconstruct) — first runs verify(), rejects conflicting same-index shard evidence, then cross-checks every committed shard hash against the supplied shard set, including role/origin/sequence/set-id/plan/payload_len/payload_hash/protocol_version agreement. When reconstruct=true it re-runs reconstruct_erasure_payload and confirms both the reproduced payload hash and byte length.

audit_ledger.semantics: Append-only and dedup-keyed on receipt_commitment. record() verifies legacy-v1 intrinsic consistency before admission, returns Ok(true) for a new receipt and Ok(false) for an idempotent duplicate. summary_hash() is a deterministic insertion-order digest. Custom deserialization verifies every intrinsic receipt, rejects duplicate commitments, and atomically rebuilds the skipped in-memory dedup index, so no manual reindex step is required. Trusted signer authorization requires the external protocol-v2 verifier and is not claimed by this v1 ledger.

performance: Receipt generation cost is O(contributing_shards) hash mixes plus one SHA-256 over the commitment preimage and one HMAC-SHA256 signature — bounded well under the 5ms per-reconstruction overhead budget for realistic fleet shard counts. Generation adds no reconstruction work beyond the single reconstruct_erasure_payload call the payload already requires.

tests.unit: crates/franken-engine/src/erasure_reconstruction_receipts.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests (generation, parity recovery, canonical ordering, metadata cross-checks, conflicting-duplicate rejection, intrinsic mutation detection, serde round-trip, deterministic commitments, atomic ledger restore/dedup, boundary plans, and structural cardinality/range rejection)
tests.integration: crates/franken-engine/tests/erasure_reconstruction_receipts_integration.rs (fleet-state reconstruction, cross-node intrinsic validation without shards, multi-set ledger accumulation, parity recovery, committed-field mutation detection, strict JSON restoration, and serde persistence)
